comment: Reason for disagreement: I disagree where the draft asserts implementability without the artefacts national platforms require. REDDHI is directionally useful but lacks SLOs, RTO/RPO, and offline/degraded-mode design. The component set omits a first-class Consent Decision capability and under-specifies ABAC/purpose-of-use, claims adjudication, and supply-chain verification. Semantic governance explains LIMR vs Terminology Service well but does not define versioning, deprecation windows, or consumer impact analysis. Conformance/testing is not practical: IHE deferral leaves new DPI-H components without reference test suites or a national/regional conformance authority model. Implementation pathways lack a hard dependency graph, legacy strangler patterns, and an institutional operating model beyond a single National Digital Architect. Financing guidance is conceptually right (recurrent infrastructure) but lacks TCO drivers and procurement gates. Cross-income applicability and country examples are too anecdotal and understate constrained-connectivity, sovereignty, and ops reality. Language is generally clear for architects, but “zero-trust,” “resilient,” and “testable architecture” are over-claimed relative to the technical depth provided.
